feature: Independently verify all 10 real baseline_action_templates write actions via #900 powerShellVerify
notes: Part of Epic #803. Triggers each of the 10 real, already-executable baseline_action_templates rows
(lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-07-20-launch-control-phase3-templates.sql) via the real
POST /admin/baseline-templates/:templateId/test route, reads back the app's OWN post-write Graph GET
(graphTests, MT_APP_CLIENT_ID read app) as the 'app-reported' value, then diffs that against
#900's powerShellVerify — a real delegated Get-*/Get-Mg* cmdlet run as Shane himself (Connect-MgGraph,
NOT the app's app-only identity) — so the verification is genuinely independent of whatever identity
performed the write. The 8 quick-start-pack templates from 0195_baseline_templates_quickstart_data.sql
are NOT covered here — that migration's absolute-URL bug (documented in the phase3 migration's own
header comment) makes them a separate, out-of-scope fix.
PRECONDITIONS Shane must satisfy before running this manifest (cannot be verified or seeded from
this headless environment — no DATABASE_URL, no live Graph access):
1. At least one tenants row with isTestbed=true, status='active', a connected tenantId, AND that
tenant's msps row has write_back_enabled=true and tenants.consent->writeBack.status='granted'
(graphWriteForTenant's two write-back gates — a missing grant throws before any Graph call is made).
2. GRAPH_TEST_TENANT_ID (BuildConsole env) must equal that same testbed tenant's real tenantId GUID —
graphTests below refuse to run against any other tenant by hard guard (GraphTestExecutor.AuthorizeAsync).
3. MT_APP_CLIENT_ID/_SECRET (read app) configured in BuildConsole's environment for the graphTests below.
4. Every REPLACE_WITH_* / literal placeholder object id below replaced with a REAL object that exists
in that testbed tenant, same pattern test-manifests/900-powershell-verify-example.json itself uses
('replace the literal user object id below with a real TESTBED user'). Suggested real seed objects:
TESTBED_USER_ID                    - a real testbed user, currently enabled, zero assigned licenses,
not yet a member of TESTBED_GROUP_ID or TESTBED_TEAM_ID
TESTBED_GROUP_ID / TESTBED_TEAM_ID - a real security/M365 group and a real Team in the testbed tenant
TESTBED_GROUP_EXISTING_MEMBER_ID   - a user ALREADY a member of TESTBED_GROUP_ID (for the remove test)
TESTBED_TEAM_EXISTING_MEMBER_USER_ID - a user ALREADY a member of TESTBED_TEAM_ID (for the remove test)
TESTBED_SKU_ID                     - a real subscribedSku GUID available (unconsumed seats) in the tenant
TESTBED_DRIVE_ID / TESTBED_RECYCLED_ITEM_ID - a real drive + an item CURRENTLY sitting in its recycle
bin (Shane must delete a throwaway test file first) — Graph has
no app-only-readable 'list recycle bin' endpoint to discover this,
so section 10 is precondition-gated the same way #891's checkout
money-path manifest is (a real precondition the harness can't seed).
5. Run `Connect-MgGraph` interactively once in a pwsh 7 window signed in as Shane (per #900) so the cached
delegated token exists before any powerShellVerify step runs.
'Remove' actions (groups.remove_member / teams.remove_member) verify ABSENCE, which this tool's
afterStep/compareField diff can't express directly (no containsNone in powerShellVerify, only exact/contains).
Both sides are written as an equivalent presence-probe returning the literal id string when still present or
'' when gone (PS7 ternary on the app side's regex-captured value, matching shape on both sides) — see the
per-step comments below. licensing.remove_license uses the same trick against TESTBED_SKU_ID.
Git #901 also required a small scope-matching fix in artifacts/api-server/src/routes/admin-baseline-templates.ts:
the testbed-customers lookup and the :templateId/test route were plain requireAdmin (session-cookie only),
which a headless #898-triggered BuildConsole run has no way to satisfy. Switched those two routes (only)
to requireAdminOrIngestToken(), the exact same bypass admin-test-trigger.ts/admin-deploy-console.ts/
admin-engines.ts already use for this identical headless-testing purpose.

apiTests.name: bootstrap: look up a real testbed customer id (real DB read, no literal placeholder needed)
4/10 licensing.assign_license - trigger real write (must run before 5/10's removal of the same sku)
5/10 licensing.remove_license - trigger real write (removes the sku 4/10 just assigned)
7/10 groups.remove_member - trigger real write (removes a DIFFERENT, already-present member so this test doesn't depend on 6/10's ordering)

9/10 teams.remove_member - trigger real write (REPLACE_WITH_REAL_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP_ID: the Teams conversationMembership id for TESTBED_TEAM_EXISTING_MEMBER_USER_ID, resolved via GET /teams/{teamId}/members and matched on userId — per the phase3 migration's own note, this is NOT the user id)
10/10 sharepoint.restore_recycle_bin_item - trigger real write (precondition-gated: driveId/itemId must be a real currently-recycled item, see notes)

graphTests.name: 1/10 app-reported: read back accountEnabled via the app's own read Graph integration

3/10 app-reported: read back signInSessionsValidFromDateTime (revokeSignInSessions stamps this to 'now' - identical underlying AAD attribute read twice, so an exact match is meaningful even across two different apps/identities)
4/10 app-reported: read back the assigned sku (assumes TESTBED_USER_ID had zero licenses before 4/10 ran, so index [0] is unambiguous)

5/10 app-reported: probe whether TESTBED_SKU_ID is still present after 5/10's removal - regex with a trailing empty-string alternative so it always resolves: captures the sku guid text if still present, or '' if genuinely gone (never an extraction failure either way)
6/10 app-reported: direct group-membership check (GET /groups/{id}/members/{id} returns the member object if it IS a direct member, 404 otherwise)

7/10 app-reported: probe whether the removed member is still present - same always-resolves regex trick as 5/10 (captures the id if still a member, '' once genuinely removed; a real 404 here is expected and fine, this reads the response body either way)

8/10 app-reported: scan the team's member list for the added user's userId (Teams conversationMembers don't support a /members/{userId} direct-lookup shortcut the way group members do, so this regexes the list body for the literal userId)
9/10 app-reported: probe whether TESTBED_TEAM_EXISTING_MEMBER_USER_ID is still in the team's member list - same always-resolves regex trick as 5/10 and 7/10
10/10 app-reported: read back the restored item's name (proves it's live again post-restore, not still 404/deleted)

powerShellVerify.name: 5/10 licensing.remove_license ground truth (same presence-or-empty-string shape as the app-side regex in graphTests 5/10)
7/10 groups.remove_member ground truth (same presence-or-empty-string shape as the app-side regex in graphTests 7/10)
9/10 teams.remove_member ground truth (same presence-or-empty-string shape as the app-side regex in graphTests 9/10)
10/10 sharepoint.restore_recycle_bin_item ground truth
